title: Sable and the Sigil
premise: Isandro Iversen, a scribe indentured to the Ledger Guild of Vharn, discovers that the guild's 'impossible things' are debts owed between realms — and the border wards fell because someone defaulted on the oldest covenant of all. Armed only with his ledgers and a stolen sigil-stamp, he must trace the covenant's broken chain across a starless land, gathering a found family of debtors, deserters, and one dying dragon who holds the final signature. The climax comes when Isandro learns the guild's master engineered the collapse to erase all debts — including Isandro's own life-bond — forcing him to choose between freedom and the realms' survival. He reforges the covenant by writing himself into it as guarantor, paying with his name from every record, and ends the book unnamed but belonging, keeper of a new ledger kept by those he saved.
about_author: Jonah Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers before turning to fantasy. They write about paperwork as magic and strangers who become kin.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A night of routine ledger-keeping in the Guild of Vharn establishes his debt-bound servitude and his gift for reading covenants no one else can parse. When a page in the oldest ledger rewrites itself mid-entry, he hides it rather than report it — a small act of theft that will define everything. Emotional beat: quiet resentment hardening into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The border wards shatter with a sound like tearing silk; every flame in the city gutters blue, then dies. In the dark, guild enforcers begin burning records — including the page Isandro stole. He flees with the ledger under his coat as the guildhouse seals itself behind him. Emotional beat: terror laced with exhilarating, unfamiliar freedom.

chapters.title: A Debtor's Welcome
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, meeting Sable. Hunted through the starless streets, he is sheltered by Sable, a ward-tinkerer who owes the guild three favors she can never repay. She recognizes the sigil-stamp hidden in his satchel and tells him what it is: a key to the old covenant between realms. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of mutual desperation.

chapters.title: What the Guild Trades In
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She explains the covenant: long ago, the human realm borrowed dragon-fire to hold back the Hollow, paying in names, years, and memory. The guild became its broker — and grew fat skimming the interest. Isandro realizes the falling wards mean someone stopped paying. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of learning your whole world runs on a loan.

chapters.title: The First Signature
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Following the ledger's self-writing pages, they reach a ruined tollhouse where the first covenant-signature was sworn. There they find Brannoc, an ex-enforcer who deserted when ordered to burn debtor villages, now guarding the site. He nearly kills them before Isandro reads his true name off a debt-page and offers to strike it clean. Emotional beat: dangerous trust extended as a gamble.

chapters.title: Road Through the Hollow-Light
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The trio travels toward the dragon-mounts, crossing country where the Hollow seeps through the fallen wards — places where forgotten things walk and memories pool like fog. Brannoc's guilt over the burned villages surfaces; Isandro quietly amends his ledger entry. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes the first thread of real fellowship.

chapters.title: The Market of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They pass through a black-market bazaar trading in covenant fragments: bottled years, secondhand courage, a cage of unspoken vows. A guild factor recognizes Isandro and raises the alarm; in the escape, Sable spends her first owed favor buying them passage — and learns the favor was promised to someone else. Emotional beat: sacrifice that costs more than intended.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They find the lowlands burning — not by dragons, but by guild fire-scribes erasing evidence of the old debts. Among the ash, Isandro meets Wren, a child left nameless when her village's covenant-page burned, who cannot remember her own mother's face. He takes her in without deciding to. Emotional beat: tenderness arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: The Master's Summons
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Master Corvane). Corvane, guild-master, reveals his design: if all covenant debts are erased, no realm holds power over another — and he alone will hold the new blank slate. He dispatches his enforcers to retrieve Isandro, whom he calls 'the last honest pen.' Emotional beat: chilling conviction; the villain believes he is merciful.

chapters.title: Where Dragons Remember
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The company climbs into the dragon-mounts and finds them near-empty — most dragons have flown beyond the wards or died keeping them lit. In a crater-shrine they meet Ysolde, last dragon of the western flight, ancient and guttering, whose fire is the covenant's living seal. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency at how little time remains.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. The dragon explains the covenant cannot be rewritten by force — it must be reaffirmed by a mortal guarantor who consents to be bound. Every previous guarantor paid with their name, their place in memory. Ysolde has waited two hundred years for someone willing. Isandro says nothing. Emotional beat: the weight of a choice being placed in small hands.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Resting in Ysolde's crater, the found family takes stock: Sable teaching Wren ward-craft, Brannoc whittling her a toy, Isandro recording each kindness in a new ledger he starts — debts freely given, freely owed. It is the happiest night any of them remembers. Emotional beat: belonging discovered before it can be threatened.

chapters.title: Enforcers at the Pass
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Corvane's enforcers find them. Brannoc holds the pass alone against his former brothers-in-arms, buying the others time to flee deeper into the mountains. He falls — but Isandro, watching from above, strikes Brannoc's death-debt from the ledger, and the wound closes enough for Sable to drag him clear. Emotional beat: love weaponized against fate itself.

chapters.title: The Blank Page Bargain
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Captured briefly by a factor, Isandro is offered his heart's desire: full pardon, his debt annulled, his freedom — if he surrenders the ledger. He sees the trap: a pardoned man is a man with no stake. He refuses and escapes through the factor's own records, rewriting his cell into a locked room. Emotional beat: choosing chains with meaning over freedom without.

chapters.title: What Sable Owes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Her remaining favors come due, and the creditor arrives to collect: her service, her craft, her future. She pays the second favor to buy Ysolde safe passage down-mountain, leaving herself bound. Isandro rages at her self-sacrifice; she answers that family means paying each other's debts without being asked. Emotional beat: fierce, painful definition of found family.

chapters.title: The Guildhouse of Vharn
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The company infiltrates the sealed guildhouse to reach the Covenant Master-Ledger before Corvane completes the erasure. Inside, shelves of names scream softly as pages burn. Isandro finds his own indenture-record and understands at last why Corvane wants him alive: a debt-bound scribe makes the perfect scapegoat guarantor. Emotional beat: horror at being a tool, resolve at refusing to be one.

chapters.title: Corvane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Confronted in the vault, Corvane lays out his logic with terrible gentleness: debts built this cruel world; erase them and no one is ever owned again. He shows Isandro the empty page where his own name would go — freedom, offered like a knife. Isandro counters that a world with no debts is a world where no one ever gave anything. Emotional beat: the thematic argument made flesh.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. As Corvane's scribes burn the Master-Ledger, Ysolde unleashes her final reserve of fire to shield it, knowing it will end her. The covenant-flame gutters to an ember held in Wren's cupped hands — the nameless child suddenly holding the last light between realms. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice, hope reduced to something small enough to carry.

chapters.title: Signature in Blood and Ash
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax. With the ember fading, Isandro writes himself into the covenant as guarantor — not with his given name, which Corvane could steal, but with the ledger of small debts: every kindness his found family recorded. The covenant accepts a bond made of belonging, not ownership. Corvane reaches to erase it and finds his own name already struck — spent long ago. Emotional beat: triumph through surrender.

chapters.title: After the Ember
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The wards rise again, faint but holding; stars return one by one. Ysolde survives as a small, dull-scaled dragon no bigger than a cat — diminished, alive, and insufferably smug. The company buries the guild's ledgers and keeps only the small one. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: The Unnamed Scribe
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The price comes due gently: Isandro's name fades from every record, every memory — even his own reflection feels like a stranger's. But Wren renames him with a word from her recovered memories, and Sable and Brannoc teach it to the world one person at a time. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into chosen identity.

chapters.title: A New Ledger Opens
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing chorus. One year later, the four — plus a cat-sized dragon — run a modest scriptorium where anyone may record a debt of gratitude, and anyone may forgive one. On the final page, Wren writes the first entry: 'We owe each other everything. Paid in full, daily.' Emotional beat: warm, earned peace — belonging as an ongoing practice.
